chapter: Hotel bands, Texas friends and the scrapbook
title: Tim Kelly, Peck Kelly and a Houston friend
summary: Talk about Tim Kelly of East Texas, the new Peck Kelly record, Riddick's meeting with Peck, and Houston friend Skipper Trevathian.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, San Antonio is where he's at. And you know who's from over there in Marshall? I guess he was born in Mississippi but moved away like you is Tim Kelly.
Is that where Tim is now? No. Someone was asking me.
No, he's in Jackson. He's retired.
That's what I understand. He was with manager of Whirlines in Jackson. But he grew up in Marshall even though he's from a Mississippi family. Yeah.
And he told me about playing around East Texas and how he went on from there to do everything.
I liked Tim very, very much. He was one fine fellow. Mm-hmm. Still is. Oh, yeah. Tim was a very good friend of Peck Kelly's.
Mm-hmm. Well, they finally put out a record of Peck. I haven't heard it yet.
See, I never heard Peck. I just got a couple, an album, a brand new album of Art Tatum's. Boy, it's a knockout. Really? Boy, he played so, so very beautifully.
Did you know Peck in Texas?

I got to the Southern Nenna Club. I was between trains in Houston. And they wouldn't let, this was just after World War II. They wouldn't let servicemen in unless they had a date. I guess they were afraid I was going to start a fight. Yeah. Or something like that. Well, somebody else did before that, and that's the reason for it all. I think if I'd gone up and explained to them.
That I knew people who knew Peck Kelly and wanted to, had been hearing about him for years. Well, a few years then.

You see, I had a very good friend over in Houston. He was manager of the piano department in Carter Music Company, Skipper Trevathian. Mm-hmm. And Skipper played piano and organ. And whenever I'd go to Houston to play at the Shamrock, well, I'd look up Skipper until Skipper passed away. Mm-hmm.
I don't know too many people over there now in the music business.
I heard one band over there. I don't know anybody in the music business anymore.
